runtime_proof.measurement_basis: The changed module executed directly at this head via tsx, plus one in-place mutation of the guard under test. No stub and no fixture: these are the real exported functions the Next.js auth callback calls. This lane performs no database access, so the runtime facts measured are identity-resolution facts, not row facts.

queries.name: an authorized login resolves to its mapped canonical id, not its local-part
queries.result: resolved capperId = 'griff843' for an address whose local-part is 'pilot.capper'
queries.significance: The identity comes from the explicit mapping. Under the previous implementation this same address would have resolved to "pilotcapper".

queries.name: an unmapped (bare email) entry admits nobody
queries.significance: There is no local-part fallback. A stale bare-email deployment value fails closed rather than admitting a derived identity.

queries.name: a non-canonical id is refused rather than repaired
queries.significance: Silent repair of an id is exactly how a wrong identity previously reached the database; the parser refuses instead.

queries.name: empty ALLOWED_CAPPER_EMAILS admits nobody
queries.significance: UTV2-1786 fail-closed behaviour is preserved by this change.

queries.name: the derivation path is removed, not merely bypassed
queries.result: exports = findAllowedCapper, normalizeEmail, parseAllowedCapperEmails; derivation helper present = false
queries.significance: No caller can reach local-part derivation, including future ones.

queries.name: mutation: restoring local-part derivation breaks the acceptance tests
queries.method: reinstated the fallback email.split('@')[0].replace(/[^a-z0-9_-]/g,'') for entries with no '=' and re-ran the suite
queries.result: # pass 7 / # fail 2 — "an entry with no explicit mapping is rejected and admits nobody" and "a non-canonical capper id is refused rather than sanitised" both failed; mutation reverted before commit
queries.significance: The tests fail on the exact condition they name, so they are load-bearing rather than decorative.
